title: Dossier header
body:
# VERIFIED STORY DOSSIER

**Re: $2.4M no-bid HVAC award (matter verification-nobid-contracts)**

Every claim below is backed by a rule application and a source span. Claims the record does not support are listed as open, not asserted.

title: The award and the price gap
body:
## 1. The award

The city awarded a **$2.4M** HVAC contract **without competitive bidding** against a **$900k budget line** — a **$1.5M overrun** — while the cheapest qualified bid on record was **$1.1M**. The contract recites "emergency procurement", but no emergency declaration has been produced.

title: Competition was thin
body:
## 2. The cheaper bids that disappeared

Two competing bids (**$1.1M** and **$1.3M**) were disqualified on technicalities — a missing signature page and an expired trade certificate — without a review memo. Both disqualifications were repairable; neither vendor was asked to cure.

title: The connection
body:
## 3. The connection

The vendor's registered address is the awarding official's home address — confirmed against the state business registry. The official's disclosure statement lists no interest in the vendor. **Two independent records support this claim; we do not publish a connection claim on one.**

title: Custody and provenance
body:
## 4. Custody and provenance

Documents: FOIA release 2026-11-02 (award notice), municipal budget ledger extract, disqualification letters, state business registry extract. Source identities are withheld from this dossier; the chain-of-custody record is committed with the case and can be produced to editors and counsel on request.

title: Methodology and limits
body:
## 5. Method and limits

Claims are derived by rule from sourced facts; each is replayable. Three independent records agree on the $2.4M figure, which is why the record-keeping-error explanation is excluded. What remains unproven — the signatory's role, and whether procurement reviewed the disqualifications — is listed as an open question, not asserted.
